title: Add Costs from Table: access, commands, rows and refused writes for VSB - Application Administrator
preconditions: Signed in to both apps with an account holding only "VSB - Application Administrator". Test project (asked at run time): one inside and one outside the role's Dataverse business-unit scope, each with CAPEX contracts and costs.
test_data: PW-<runId>-AC-ACC (one month value on an in-scope project; an edit attempt on the out-of-scope project)
steps:
1. Run steps 2-n in the Canvas app first and note the result (reference).
2. On the in-scope project open DEVEX/CAPEX (left navigation " DEVEX/CAPEX") and click "Add Cost from Table"; also open /costs/add-from-table?category=<n> with projectId (code app).
3. Record which commands are visible and enabled: Add Row, Delete Row, Copy Table, Save, Cancel, close icon (and the code-app "Show all years" switch).
4. Record the contract rows listed for the category.
5. Add "PW-<runId>-AC-ACC" with metadata and one month, Save, read back, then delete it again.
6. On the out-of-scope project try the same Save (or the same edit on a contract the role cannot write).
expected: The sheet is reachable from DEVEX/CAPEX and by deep link. The role changes nothing in the screen: no Cost screen, command or gate reads gblCurrentUser, so every command has the same visible/enabled state as in the canvas for this user. Rows listed = the canvas rows for this user (Dataverse BU scope). An in-scope Save persists (with Owning Business Unit = project BU). A write outside the role's scope is refused by Dataverse and shown as an error (canvas: Notify "Something went wrong saving the Capex data. Please refresh the page and verify your changes were saved correctly."; code app: that text in the banner or the Read-only state), never as a silent success or as "no rows".
acceptance: Command states equal the canvas for the same user AND row set equals the canvas row set AND in-scope write read back with project BU AND out-of-scope write refused with a visible error AND 0 rows changed on the out-of-scope project.
